display_name: The whole Accident Compensation Act 2001 (NZ) under one top-level goal — for this injury, is there cover, what class of injury is it, which Account pays, and what weekly compensation follows — and six goals: cover, claims, entitlements, reviews and appeals, levies, offences
scope: Every provision of the Act as printed in the PCO's version 249 as at 10 July 2026 (Parts 1-11, Schedules 1AA, 1-8). Inputs: the Corporation's, Minister's and courts' discretions; regulations; indexed amounts (ss 115-116); minimum weekly earnings; Schedules 2, 3, 3A membership; facts. Carried as text: the provisions listed in each module. NOT encoded: nothing in the Act.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-12 (tests-independent.l4, 315 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read). It found seven errors: cover abroad under ss 21, 21B and 22(3)-(4), s 17(3), s 35(1)(b), the s 250(4) day count, and a non-earner's weekly compensation. Its report also found s 228(3) missing from the goal. All are fixed, and 315/315 now pass. Weekly compensation through the goal assumes permanent employment (cl 34). The source text was extracted from the PCO PDF; the PDF is not deposited. The pipeline has not been run. On 2026-10-17, at the user's direction, Legislation Act 2019 s 55 was applied to the deadlines for lodging a claim (s 53), deciding claims (ss 54-57), deciding the need for a rehabilitation plan (s 75), applying for review (s 135), the review decision (s 144), paying review costs (s 148), appealing (s 151) and seeking leave (s 162), the Corporation's list for the Registrar (s 152), recovering levies (s 226), a ceasing employer's notice (s 232), laying a charge (s 336) and an estate's application (s 120); not the s 146 deemed decision, whose date is tied to the 3 months; 4 independent assertion(s) written before that change now fail by design.

forks.F2: ss 28(5), 228(3): a treatment injury from treatment for a work injury is work-related, paid by the Work Account.
forks.F3: s 17(3): the 183-day test applies to a person who is absent.
forks.F4: Schedule 1 cl 34(1): weeks 2-5 use the 4-week figure.
forks.F5: Schedule 1 cl 56: the regulated lump sum, kept within $2,500-$100,000.
forks.F6: s 313(1): the calendar year of the offence.
forks.F7: s 121(2): lump sums barred while in prison.
forks.F8: s 22(3)-(4): for a treatment injury abroad, residence when the treatment was given; provider equivalence folded into `caused by treatment`.
forks.F9: ss 21(2)(b), 21B(2)(c): place and residence are those of the act or event.
forks.S55: Legislation Act 2019 s 55 (applied 2026-10-17 at the user's direction): the deadlines for lodging a claim (s 53), deciding claims (ss 54-57), deciding the need for a rehabilitation plan (s 75), applying for review (s 135), the review decision (s 144), paying review costs (s 148), appealing (s 151) and seeking leave (s 162), the Corporation's list for the Registrar (s 152), recovering levies (s 226), a ceasing employer's notice (s 232), laying a charge (s 336) and an estate's application (s 120); not the s 146 deemed decision, whose date is tied to the 3 months run to the next working day (Legislation Act s 13, with the Matariki dates in Schedule 1 of the Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022) when they end on a non-working day.
